name: Turn off printing support
summary: Stop and disable the Print Spooler service if you never print.
what: Stops the Print Spooler and sets it to Disabled. Microsoft offered this as a workaround for the 2021 PrintNightmare flaw where printing is not needed.
benefit: Removes a service that has been a target of serious attacks, and frees a little memory.
risk: Medium. Nothing can print from this PC, locally or over the network, and Print to PDF stops working. Revert sets the start type back.
advice: Only if you never print and never use Print to PDF. If you just want to keep others out, use Stop other computers printing through this PC instead.
facts: Microsoft's advisory says this disables printing both locally and remotely
Microsoft lists Print Spooler as OK to disable and Automatic by default
Stops the service now and keeps it from starting at the next boot
Revert puts back the start type that was there before

name: Turn off the Downloaded Maps Manager
summary: Stop the service that keeps offline maps up to date for the Maps app.
what: Sets the Downloaded Maps Manager service to Disabled. Windows uses it only for maps downloaded for offline use.
benefit: One less background service that starts with Windows.
risk: Low. Offline maps used by the Maps app stop updating and may stop working.
advice: Suggested if you do not use offline maps in the Windows Maps app.
facts: Microsoft lists it as OK to disable and Automatic by default
Only the Maps app and other apps that use downloaded maps need it
Revert puts back the start type that was there before

name: Turn off distributed link tracking
summary: Stop the service that follows moved files for old shortcuts and linked documents.
what: Sets the Distributed Link Tracking Client service to Disabled. It keeps links between NTFS files working after a file is moved.
benefit: One less background service. On a test PC it used about 1 MB while running.
risk: Low. A shortcut or linked document may no longer find a file that was moved to another drive or PC. Most people never notice.
advice: Your choice. The saving is small. It matters mainly if you want fewer services running.
facts: Microsoft lists it as OK to disable and Automatic by default
Only affects links that must follow a file that was moved
Revert puts back the start type that was there before

name: Turn off the Connected Devices Platform
summary: Stop the service behind sharing with nearby devices and linking phones and other devices.
what: Sets the Connected Devices Platform Service to Disabled. Windows uses it to connect to and share with other devices.
benefit: One less background service that talks to nearby devices. On a test PC it used a few megabytes while running.
risk: Low. Sharing with nearby devices and features that link this PC to a phone or other device may stop working.
advice: Suggested if you do not share with nearby devices or link a phone. Skip it if you do.
facts: Microsoft lists it as OK to disable and Automatic by default
Phone link is switched off separately by Turn off Phone link
Revert puts back the start type that was there before

name: Turn off UPnP and SSDP device discovery
summary: Stop the services that find and talk to UPnP devices on your network.
what: Sets the SSDP Discovery and UPnP Device Host services to Disabled. They start only when something asks for them.
benefit: Fewer network services that other devices on your network can reach.
risk: Low. Windows can no longer discover some network media players, speakers and similar UPnP devices, and apps that rely on that discovery may not find them.
advice: Suggested if you do not stream to or from network devices that use UPnP. Skip it if you do.
facts: Microsoft lists both as OK to disable and Manual by default
They only start on demand, so the gain is a smaller attack surface, not memory
Revert puts back the start type that was there before

name: Turn off Xbox Live services
summary: Stop the services for Xbox sign-in, cloud saves and Xbox networking.
what: Sets the Xbox Live Auth Manager, Xbox Live Game Save and Xbox Live Networking services to Disabled.
benefit: Three fewer services that talk to Xbox Live. They start only when an Xbox feature asks for them.
risk: Low. Signing in to Xbox, cloud saves for Xbox games and Xbox multiplayer stop working until you revert.
advice: Suggested if you do not use the Xbox app, Game Pass or Xbox games on this PC. Skip it if you do.
facts: Microsoft lists all three as should be disabled and Manual by default
Xbox accessory support is a separate service that this setting leaves alone
They only start on demand, so the gain is fewer Xbox Live connections, not memory
Revert puts back the start type that was there before

name: Turn off smart card services
summary: Stop the services that read smart cards and apply their removal rules.
what: Sets the Smart Card, Smart Card Device Enumeration and Smart Card Removal Policy services to Disabled.
benefit: Three fewer services for a feature most PCs never use.
risk: Low. Smart cards and security keys that sign in as a smart card, including some banking and work card readers, stop working.
advice: Suggested if you have no smart card reader and do not use a smart card style security key. Skip it if you do.
facts: Microsoft lists all three as OK to disable and Manual by default
They only start on demand, so the gain is a smaller attack surface, not memory
Revert puts back the start type that was there before
